text:
maria: Quick share — saw ~12% token throughput drop on Mixtral 8-bit path when FlashAttention was chosen for head_size=48. Root cause looks like padding + KV copy churn. Anyone seen this?

tom: which model/config and can you paste the profile output?

maria: mixtral-base-8bit, head_size=48, rope_scale=1.0, quant=nf4. Short profile excerpt: 
```
[PROFILE] kernel_select: Attempted FlashAttention
[PROFILE] flash_forward: 0.40 ms
[PROFILE] decision: mask detected -> switch to SDPA fallback path
[PROFILE] kv_copy: 1.20 ms (host<->device)
[PROFILE] total_step: 3.40 ms
```
End-to-end shows Flash chosen then an expensive fallback causing extra memcopies.

jay: that smells like the mask handling bug for non-aligned head sizes. Our Flash kernels assume head_size % 8 == 0 for vectorized mask ops; when head_size==48 it triggers path that ends up forcing a per-batch mask rewrite and then SDPA fallback. Also note RoPE scaling can change internal tiling (we saw weird seqlen alignment effects when rope_scale != 1.0).

perf-bot: /perf/mixtral/8bit regression detected: throughput -12.1% (p=0.02) vs baseline at 1801234000. Canary: 3/5 nodes flagged.

elaine: Quick mitigation suggestion: in kernel-selector prefer Triton/SDPA when head_size is not 16-aligned, or round pad to next 16 for Flash only after verifying mask-safe path. Also add a cheap check: if mask is dense-identity (no per-token masking) then allow Flash even if head_size%16!=0.

maria: Agree. Also seeing KV cache churn when batch_size>1 and prefix cache used — we memcpy entire KV window instead of delta-appending. Logs show: 
```
KV_COPY_BYTES before: 1.2MB
KV_COPY_BYTES after: 4.8MB (batch=4, prefix_rate=0.9)
```
So batching + prefix-heavy workloads blow up host<->device traffic.

tom: do we have incremental-kv enabled for quantized path? IIRC incrementalkv was disabled for certain Triton kernels.

jay: Right. incrementalkv was gated off for nvrtc/triton fallback to avoid pointer aliasing issues. We can reintroduce a safe incremental writer that writes only new rows when prefix_rate > 0.75. Also the batching heuristic should prefer smaller per-batch token grouping when prefix_rate is high.

elaine: Proposed patch sketch: 
```diff
- if head_size % 16 != 0: prefer_flash = false
+ if head_size % 16 != 0 and not mask_is_identity(): prefer_flash = false

# batching heuristic
if prefix_rate > 0.8 and batch_size > 1:
  use_incremental_kv = true
  target_tokens_per_batch = max(1, floor(tokens_per_gpu / 4))
```
This avoids big KV memcopies and reduces the amount of kernel fallback churn.

maria: I'll prototype the kernel-selector change + incremental KV writer. Running a matrix overnight: head_size in [48,64,80], rope_scale in [0.9,1.0,1.1], kernels=[flash,sdpa,triton], batch=[1,4]. Will upload perf traces.

tom: also let's add a unit test that asserts no Flash->SDPA runtime fallback happens for a given config set, and fail the presubmit if fallback occurs unexpectedly.

perf-bot: Note: schedule rollback threshold: if regression > 10% on canary -> auto rollback. Current canary at 5% traffic.

maria: ack. If the patch looks risky, we can expose runtime flag: redwood.runtime.force_kernel=sdpa for immediate customer rollbacks.

jay: long-term we should make kernel selection cost-aware: add estimated_kv_copy_cost to the cost model so the selector prefers a slightly slower kernel with zero-copy KV when prefix_rate high.

elaine: +1. Also add a telemetry field: kernel_fallback_reason to trace which condition triggered SDPA. That will help triage regressions automatically.

maria: I'll post the trace bundle here when finished (expect results by 1801237900). Thanks all. :thumbsup:
